title: Later Han
capsule: The Later Han (後漢, 947–950/979) was the shortest-lived of the Five Dynasties, founded by Liu Zhiyuan, a Shatuo Turk general who had governed Hedong under the Later Jin and seized the imperial throne at Kaifeng when the Khitan Liao withdrew after destroying the Later Jin in 947. Liu Zhiyuan died in 948 after less than a year on the throne; his son Liu Chengyou proved erratic and was overthrown and killed by his own generals in 950, after which Guo Wei — the military strongman behind the throne — founded the Later Zhou. A rump state, the Northern Han, survived in Taiyuan until 979.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core domain of the Later Han — the Yellow River plain — is well attested; peripheral areas were contested by warlords, and nominal suzerainty over regional powers is difficult to map precisely.
